items.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024
items.q: I might have said I would love to play piano for an artist I admire, like a Joni Mitchell.

ctx.x: So my dad was a high school band director and there was lots of instruments laying around our house. I inherited perfect pitch from him and you know I thought I was being bad when parents were over the house and I was putting together all the instruments trying to figure out how to play them. You know I thought I was some kind of criminal. But so music came naturally to me as a child, which was great, I mean what a blessing. And then I kind of got into high school and I was just playing all the time, flute and…

me. And yeah, one thing led to another and I ended up getting that job. And like I said, I kind of fell into it and it’s always been interesting to me because I had a therapist once who talked about the fact that many women, maybe not so much now but at least when I was growing up — were, as she put it, “contingency oriented.” We go from contingency to contingency dealing with each thing as it comes along instead of going, “I want to be Joni Mitchell’s musical director” or whatever that might be. And so I kind of…
That’s a good way to put it. I think I’m that way as well, like opportunities come that I hadn’t thought about doing that, but I’ll give it a try.
